## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [11. Dezember 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.71
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.71
- Datum: 11.12.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Rio, 11.12.40
Dear Hanna + Manfred, Finally we had a letter from
you after more than 3 weeks without mail. In the meantime
you seem to have moved into your new flat, and I hope
you can stay there as long as you like. What did you do with
your maid, could you take her to Bath? Whom are you going
to take instead of Mrs Youngman and her children? I am
very glad, Hanna, that you wrote about yourselves, because I
want to know as much as possible about your life, and
there are still lots of questions which I could put you. For
instance, who is Frank? I thought you had Erwin there and I
cannot think of any Frank I know. From your brother we had a
letter, thanking us, but I hope he does not travel now
during the cold season, should he go, one of Stefan's tweed
suits might be useful. - As to my dear Brother's letter: help
him with money if you think he needs it and as you say
yourself, he might be really at the end of his ressources.
As to the Brazilian visa, I do not think it will be possible. As
they do not give visas now as a rule it would mean giving a
personal guarantee and that is the only thing I cannot ask of
Stefan in this case. I shall write him next week, should you
see him before tell him we think it over and give him
something if you think he needs it. I think I shall also write
to mama, and don't you worry too much about it. I know
what it means beginning to help him, but we were not sus-
prised - it had to come one day. - Forgive if I do not
write more to-day, it is already late for posting, and
it is hot. I hope for a thunderstorm to-night and
then I shall write more at length. Keep well and
induce Manfred to stay as long as possible with you
in Bath.
Yours Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Zeile 'of 6.11.' wurde oben rechts nachträglich eingefügt. Die Tinte ist violett.
Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
I join a few lines on this famous paper which would be more
convenient for other purposes. Rio is and will always remain
the most beautiful town of the world, even such a
uncnthusiastic being as Lotte finds it wonderful. All would be
ideal here without the heat {in summer} as there are already flats with
aircooling I think it over if it should be necessary for my health
to go to a southern climat. And how far is this world from
from America! One can write only by air mail
and that won't mean for me never to send manuscripts
and for Lotte to write still shorter letters than usual. My Spanish
makes good progress and I like the language enormously - the
easiest perhaps of all Latin ones and I wonder what they will
say in Buenos Aires when I am lecturing in Spanish.
Here we live a very quiet live, I do my best to continue
this retirement after having seen so many people and if
I am giving a lecture I will do it on the last days. I
have not heard a word from Europe since months ex-
cept your letters and also from America I hear nearly
nothing, but I do not complain, all personal things
being quite indifferent now. For Friedental I can
do nothing from here except if he would like to live
here, all correspondence has no effect in America, one
has to phone and phone every day and to run. A few
weeks ago it would have been much easier, but he never
mentioned his intention. Thanks for all Stefan Zweig

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Die Handschrift von Lotte und Stefan Zweig ist klar. Die wenigen Korrekturen (wie 'in summer') wurden entsprechend der Vorgaben als Einfügungen markiert.
